channel.title: Livable Telluride — Weekly Digest
channel.description: This week's upcoming Gov-Hub meetings and community events across the Telluride region (Town of Telluride, Mountain Village, San Miguel County, the Sheridan Opera House, The Alibi, Wilkinson Library, KOTO, telluride.com, and more).

item.title: 📅 The Week Ahead — Jul 22–28
item.description: The most consequential action this week happens Wednesday, when SMART's board votes on two vendor contracts — one for gondola structural analysis, one for cabin structural analysis — that will shape whether the aging gondola has a future. That same day, Town Planning and Zoning takes up the Carhenge Redevelopment Project, a large-scale subdivision consolidation on Town-owned land at 700 W Pacific, along with other Town-initiated development concepts in the Accommodations 2 zone. Rounding out the week, the Town Council sits as Liquor Licensing Authority Sunday to hear KOTO Radio's permit request for its Live at the Drive event.

item.title: ⚡ [Meeting] Planning & Zoning Commission - Jul 23 2026 — 2026-07-23
item.description:
Town of Telluride • 2026-07-23
Three Town-owned development projects dominate this agenda — all in the Accommodations 2 zone, all designed by Design Workshop, all on land the Town itself owns. The Carhenge Redevelopment Project gets two bites of the apple: a Preliminary Large Scale Subdivision to consolidate Lots 34 and 34B at 700 W Pacific Ave into a single parcel over 15,000 sq ft, and a Conceptual PUD for new construction on that consolidated lot (carried over from May). Separately, the Shandoka Lot at 860 Black Bear Rd gets its own Conceptual PUD hearing for proposed new construction on the Town's 4.07-acre parcel. Both sites sit at the center of the ongoing question about what Telluride does with its open-space-adjacent Town properties. Also on: a Minor Subdivision at 238 N Pine Street in the Historic Residential zone — a 7,500 sq ft or smaller parcel proposed to be split into two lots, a request that has been continued multiple times since February.
⚡ Why it matters: Town-owned Carhenge site up for subdivision consolidation and concept review.

item.title: ⚡ [Meeting] San Miguel Authority for Regional Transportation - Jul 23 2026 — 2026-07-23
item.description:
Town of Telluride • 2026-07-23
SMART's board meets virtually on July 23rd with the gondola project front and center. Two vendor selections are up for action: Resolution 2026-12 would award SCJ Alliance the contract for gondola structural analysis, and Resolution 2026-13 would award the Gondola Shop the cabin structural analysis work — separate contracts, same bridge-or-bust question. The board will also discuss the composition of the Gondola Advisory Committee, get a broader project update, and hear introduction of a FY26 budget amendment. Rounding out the agenda: second-quarter performance and July operations reports, the executive director's verbal update, and an executive session on personnel matters.
⚡ Why it matters: Two vendor contract votes decide who analyzes the gondola's structural future.

item.title: [Thu, Jul 23] DIY Condiments with Kayla
item.description:
🎫 KOTO 📍 Wilkinson Public Library, Telluride
Skip the store-bought bottles and discover how easy—and delicious—it is to make your own flavorful condiments from scratch. Join fermentation educator and local food advocate Kayla Wexelberg of Taste Your Roots for a hands-on workshop focused on creating homemade condiments and barbecue sauce using fresh, wholesome ingredients. Learn the fundamentals of balancing sweet, salty, tangy, and savory flavors while crafting customizable recipes that fit your taste and dietary preferences. Participants will explore ingredient combinations, discover simple techniques for elevating everyday meals, and leave with recipes and inspiration to continue experimenting at home. Whether you're a backyard grill master, a home cook looking to expand your kitchen skills, or simply curious about making more foods from scratch, this class will help you add a personal touch to every meal.

item.title: [Thu, Jul 23] Emotional Regualtion Workshop w/Betsy Lamberson
item.description:
🎫 KOTO 📍 Wilkinson Public Library, Telluride
In this two-hour workshop, participants will learn to work with their nervous system to navigate challenging times and build self-regulation skills unique to their situation. Participants will create their own self-care compass that helps them to navigate stress and identify what measures could be restorative to their nervous systems. There will be a mix of presentation, writing prompts, and group discussion. Betsy Lamberson is a parenting educator and nervous system coach who helps caregivers and professionals better understand behavior through the lens of stress and connection. Through her work at New Roots Parenting, she offers practical, neuroscience-informed tools rooted in co-regulation, self-awareness, and relationship repair. www.newrootsparenting.com
